t: Minimum Time to Type Word Using Special Typewriter — Shortest Hop Around a 26-Key Ring
o: The letters form a circle of 26 keys; typing the key under the pointer costs one second and each single-key move, clockwise or counterclockwise, costs one second. Between two consecutive characters of word only the circular distance matters, and on a cycle the shortest route is min(clockwise, counterclockwise). For "abc" the pointer starts at a: type (1s), step to b (1s), type (1s), step to c (1s), type (1s) — 5 seconds total. For "bza" the hop b to z takes 2 steps counterclockwise rather than 24 clockwise, giving 2 + 3 + 2 = 7. Since each character genuinely requires one type action no matter what, only movement is negotiable, and a single pass adding min-distance plus one per character is optimal.
k: Total time decomposes greedily: sum of shortest circular distances between consecutive letters, plus exactly |word| typing seconds.
For letters d apart on a 26-ring the cost is min(d, 26 - d) — never walk the long way around.
Typing costs a fixed 1 second per character; only movement between characters can be optimized.

a.i: Track the previously typed letter, starting from a. For each character take d as the plain absolute index difference; the circular distance is min(d, 26 - d). Add that movement cost plus one typing second per character.
s: Keep prev initialized to the character a.
For each character c compute d = |index(c) - index(prev)|.
Add min(d, 26 - d) + 1 to the running total.
Set prev = c and continue; return the total at the end.
a.t: O(n) — one pass with constant work per character

a.i: Same idea expressed with modular arithmetic: normalize the signed gap into [0, 26) so it reads directly as clockwise steps, then the counterclockwise alternative is simply 26 minus that value. Equivalent output, slightly more idiomatic when positions are already integer indices.
s: Convert letters to indices 0..25, initializing prev to 0 (the letter a).
Compute d = (cur - prev) mod 26, the clockwise distance.
a.t: O(n) — identical single pass with constant work per character

w: Either version answers this cleanly in an interview; name the ring-distance lemma explicitly before coding. Pitfalls: walking the long arc (b to z is 2 steps, not 24), chaining distances from the wrong anchor — the pointer rests where the previous character was typed — and forgetting the pointer starts at a rather than at your first character. Follow-ups: a rectangular keyboard grid (switch to Manhattan distance), or weighted moves where some directions cost more.
